name: Tidikelt-Tuat Tamazight
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only wordlists (Basset 1887, Rohlfs 1864/65); Kossmann survey pages, no stress-covering description found

sources.citation: Boudjellal, Malek. 2025. Notes linguistiques sur le zénète du Gourara. Iles d Imesli 17(1): 59-69. [neighbouring Gourara variety, separate Glottolog languoid]
sources.note: Nothing; the phonetics part treats consonantism (absence of spirantisation, k>c, g>j, no labiovelarisation). Its literature review confirms Gourara/Touat Zenati 'n'a pas bénéficié d'une exploration linguistique approfondie'.

sources.citation: Kossmann, Maarten. 2020. Berber subclassification. In R. Vossen & G. J. Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages, pp. 281-289 (Touat/Tidikelt at pp. 283-284). Oxford: OUP.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: printed p. 285, section on the seven-block classification
sources.note: This work describes Berber as a family (survey/subclassification chapter). Names the Zenatic block incl. the Saharan oases Figuig, Gourara, Mzab, Ouargla; Tidikelt/Touat are not named anywhere in the chapter. The chapter never mentions Tidikelt or Touat. Its only prosodic statement is the family-level claim that the accentual system was lost in all non-Tuareg varieties of Algeria and Morocco; it would cover Tidikelt only by the outside premise that Tidikelt is a non-Tuareg Algerian oasis variety, which the file itself does not state. No Tidikelt data, no stress placement, no secondary stress,…
sources.venue: The Oxford Handbook of African Languages

sources.citation: Kossmann, Maarten. 2020. Proto-Berber phonological reconstruction: An update. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 6: 11-42. Sec. 12 'The accent', para. 99.
sources.note: Family-level generalisation only: 'Berber languages of Morocco and Algeria (except Tuareg) do not seem to have a system of word accent. Instead, accentual features are governed by higher level prosodic organization, which one could call intonation.' Touat/Tidikelt not named; no data or source for this variety.

sources.citation: Bouhania, Bachir. 2010. Assessing the ethno-/socio-linguistic vitality of 'Arabic', French, and Zenete in the Touat. Cahiers de Linguistique et Didactique 3(1): 59-84.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic vitality survey, bibliography contains no descriptive work on Touat Zenati.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page tidi1241 (refs: Kossmann 1999: 31-32; Kossmann 2013: 21-24; Kossmann 2020: 283-284 for classification; no Glottolog's most extensive description).
Basset, André (1959). La langue berbère au Sahara. In Articles de dialectologie berbère, pp. 33-45 (orig. Cahiers Charles de Foucauld 10, 1948, pp. 115-127).
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: maps at printed pp. 38-41 of the 1959 volume
sources.note: This work describes Berber in the Sahara as a whole: the Tuareg dialects (Kel Ahaggar, Ioullemmeden, Idaousak, Ghat, Djanet), Zenaga, and the sedentary ksour dialects listed east to west (Siwa, Aoudjila, Sokna, Ghadames, Oued Righ, Ouargla, Ngousa, Mzab, Goura. General survey of Berber in the Sahara (vitality, Arabic contact, Tuareg vs. ksour dialects, vocabulary, verb morphology, tifinagh). Tidikelt is mentioned once as the location of the single Berber-speaking village Tit. No statement anywhere on word stress, accent, or tone; a full-text search for stress/accent/ton/tonique/intonation/syl…

sources.citation: Basset, André. 1941. La langue berbère dans les territoires du Sud. Revue Africaine 85: 62-71 (also A. Basset 1959, 'La langue berbère au Sahara', Articles de dialectologie berbère, pp. 33-45).
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.locator: printed p. 62; Touat/Tidikelt also named in the list of René Basset's 1883-1887 documentation on printed p. 63
sources.note: This work describes Berber varieties of the Algerian Territoires du Sud as a whole (survey): ksours of the Sud oranais, Touat (Tementit, Tittaf), Tidikelt (Tit), Gourara, Mzab, Ouargla/Ngousa, Oued Righ (Temasin etc.), Ghat/Djanet sedentaries, and the northern. The article is a survey (distribution of Berber-speaking points in the Territoires du Sud, history of studies, the author's 1932-1939 linguistic-atlas enquiry, four lexical sketch maps on pp. 64-65 and 68-69, remarks on dialect grouping, Tuareg lexical conservatism, borrowing and toponymy, plus a bibliographic supplement on p. 71). Tou…

sources.citation: Basset, René. 1887. Notes de lexicographie berbère, 4e série: Vocabulaire du Touat et du Gourara, argot du Mzab, dialecte des Touaregs Aouelimmiden. Journal Asiatique 8e sér., t. 10: 365-464 (offprint bound in 'Notes de lexicographie berbère', archive.org item NotesDeLexicographieBerbre). Sec. II 'Phonétique et morphologie', offprint pp. 24-28.
sources.note: Nothing. The phonetics section (informants from Tementit, Tiattaf, Badrian, Timissakht in Touat and Timimoun in Gourara) covers only consonant correspondences (palatalised t/d, r > h' before consonant, g/j/ch alternations, final-consonant loss in Gourari); no mention of accent, and transcriptions carry no accent marks.
